# dsh-outline
简体中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that searches and reads an Outline knowledge base from your conversation.
Give it a keyword — it returns matching documents with **titles, snippets, and links**; ask for one
of them and it returns the **full content in Markdown**. Approved write tools can create, update, an
d delete documents, with an approval prompt before every write.
> Project status: 0.9.2. The current feature set is covered by unit tests (233 tests with cross-plat
form edge cases), a Mock-server smoke, and a settings-chain integration check. Supported platforms:
Windows / macOS / Linux. The supported DSH baseline is `0.1.5-rc.2` (`settings.installSection` is re
quired for the settings card); the dsh `0.2.x` line (`>=0.2.0-rc.1 <1.0.0`) is also adapted, verifie
d through `0.2.2-rc.1`. Older Harness builds are not certified.

## Outline version compatibility
The plugin talks to eight core endpoints (`documents.search|list|info|create|update|delete`, `collec
tions.list`, `users.list`), whose request and response shapes have stayed the same from `v0.79` thro
ugh `v1.12`. What does change across versions is a few request parameters, and the plugin adapts at
runtime instead of pinning one version's syntax:

| Append to document body | `append: true` | `editMode: "append"` | `editMode: "append"` |
| Collect
ion / author filter | top-level `collectionId` / `userId` | same (deprecated) | `filters` array, **m

utually exclusive** with the legacy keys |
| Time filter (`updatedAfter`) | not supported by the ser
ver | not supported | `filters` with `updatedAt` + `gte` |
How that is handled:
- **Append sends both keys.** With `append: true` the request carries `append: true` *and* `editMode
: "append"`. Older servers ignore `editMode`; newer ones convert `append` into `editMode` and delete
it. Sending only one of them silently degrades to a **full overwrite** on the other side — no error

, just replaced content, which is why both are always sent.
- **Time filtering is probed once per in
stance.** A `documents.list` with a future-dated `updatedAt` filter tells the plugin whether the ser
ver honours `filters` (empty result = yes, real total = the field was stripped). Supported instances
get the filter pushed down and return `timeFilterMode: "server"`; older ones have the page filtered
locally and return `timeFilterMode: "client"`; when the query is **empty**, it instead pages throug
h `documents.list` (naturally ordered by `updatedAt` descending) and stops at the time boundary, ret
urning `timeFilterMode: "list"` — exact, one request. The legacy server has no `updatedAfter` parame

ter at all — it never existed in any Outline release, so there is nothing to send.
- **Collection /
author filtering keeps the top-level keys**, which every version accepts. They are deprecated in 1.1
2+ but not removed; the `filters` path is entered only when a time filter is also requested, because
the server rejects the two combined.
### Workflow: writing a requirement document (common task)
See the full SOP: `docs/workflow-requirement-doc.zh.md` — locate the directory (`outline_resolve_pat
h`) → fetch the template (`outline_doc_template`) → draft → create with approval → verify.
## Security
Every write goes through native DSH approval and a per-deployment directory allow-list, and both fai
l closed: an unavailable approval service, an error inside the gate, or an unresolvable target path
all refuse the write instead of performing it. On top of that the plugin registers the host's **mono
tonic guard** (`ctx.tools.guard`) as a floor: unlike the reorderable `tools/pre-execute` waterfall i
t cannot be overridden by any listener, so writes are still refused even if the gate is short-circui
ted by another plugin or never installed at all. Public instances must use HTTPS (loopback and priva
te intranet hosts are exempt), API tokens stay in the DSH settings layer and never reach tool output
, logs, or the browser half, and `outline_delete` asks for a second confirmation (the second prompt
is raced against the caller's signal, so cancelling the turn aborts it) and only reports success whe
n the server explicitly says so — an unconfirmable result is reported as an error, never as "deleted
". Local Markdown saves are confined to the configured save directory and refuse disk roots, filesys
tem roots, share roots and known system directories; that is a seatbelt, not a sandbox. The check ru
ts, share roots and known system directories; that is a seatbelt, not a sandbox. The check ru [长行截断]
> **With the approval policy set to "never", every write is refused.** That is DSH's designed fail-c
losed behaviour (no approver available means deny), not a plugin fault. Switch the policy back to "a
sk" to allow writes.
See SECURITY.md for the full threat model and for how to report a vulnerability privately.
## Cross-platform compatibility
Windows, macOS and Linux are all first-class targets; every key code path is platform-agnostic and C
I verifies Node 22 / 24 across all three operating systems. Nothing needs to be configured per platf
rifies Node 22 / 24 across all three operating systems. Nothing needs to be configured per platform.
**Windows**
- Backslash input is normalized to forward slashes, so `Collection A\Dir 1` resolves like `Collectio

n A/Dir 1`.
- Filenames are sanitized — characters illegal on Windows are replaced and reserved devi
ce names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1-9`, `LPT1-9`) are rewritten — and leading/trailing dots and spaces are

normalized so names cannot be silently trimmed.
- Paths that would exceed the Windows `MAX_PATH` li

mit (260) are truncated while preserving the `.md` extension.
